notes: Direct HTTP fetch (curl) sufficed for the whole investigation; Magento 2 site, no Claude-specific robots.txt disallow (robots.txt body was effectively empty/allow-all). Discovery method: fetched the 3-part sitemap index (sitemap_pages.xml, sitemap_collections.xml [231 URLs = real taxonomy/CMS category list], sitemap_products.xml [7471 product URLs, used as total-catalog denominator for proportion checks]) plus the homepage mega-menu HTML, then content-sampled every holiday-looking URL rather than trusting titles/slugs. Verified real routes are genuine (not universal fake-alias pages) by requesting a nonsense slug (/totally-fake-holiday-xyz123.html), which correctly 404'd, vs. every real candidate URL below returning HTTP 200. Searched sitemap+nav for Christmas, Diwali, Halloween, Easter, Valentine's, Thanksgiving, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan/Rakhi, Eid, Hanukkah, Mother's Day, Father's Day. RESULT - only ONE genuine seasonal category found: 'Rakhi's' (/rakhi-s.html), a real PLP under Raksha Bandhan - has a live breadcrumb (HOME > Rakhi's), a real layered-nav toolbar ('0 items', Sort By, clear all filters) matching the markup pattern of confirmed real category pages (compared against /dining/mugs-cups-saucers/mugs.html which uses the same product-block/plp-NNNNN markup), and body copy specifically about Rakhi thread bracelets for Raksha Bandhan ('This Rakshabandhan, tie a pious knot of affection for your brother with the lovingly handcrafted collection of Rakhis...send rakhi to India'). Site-reported qty is currently 0 (legit-zero: real taxonomy node, just out of season/restocking - Raksha Bandhan already passed for 2026 as of this Sept 4 check) - included per instructions since exact site-reported qty is a valid outcome even at zero. EXCLUDED after content-sampling (looked genuine by URL/title but failed content verification): (1) /diwali-gifting.html and /raksha-bandhan-gift-shop - both return HTTP 200 but their CMS body is empty (only global nav/footer boilerplate, zero product markup, no page-specific text) - dead/inactive campaign landing pages, not live categories. (2) /diwali-gifting-edit.html and its 6 sub-pages (copper-steel-edit, tea-coffee-edit, bamboo-edit, dinnerware-edit, wall-art-edit, decor-edit) - each shows a fixed 12-item curated grid, but every sampled product is generic home/dining decor (steel bowls, cup-and-saucer sets, bamboo cups, cushion covers, canvas wall art) with zero Diwali-specific items (no diyas, torans, rangoli, festive lighting, puja thali) - a generic-catalog gift-guide reusing standard SKUs under a Diwali marketing banner, not a genuine occasion category. (3) /valentines-day-gifts.html (245 items) and /mothers-day-special-offers.html (511 items) - both are real toolbar-driven PLPs (Sort By / clear all present) and their fractions of the 7471-product catalog are modest (3.3% and 6.8%, below the 20-30% red-flag threshold), BUT content sampling disqualifies them: requesting page 2 (?p=2) returned byte-identical product listings to page 1 for both, meaning the large advertised counts do not correspond to real distinct browsable inventory; and the actual rendered products are IDENTICAL generic bestseller SKUs shared across both pages (same porcelain oval/cylindrical mug sets, jar candles, table runners) with no Valentine's or Mother's Day-specific merchandise (no hearts/roses/couple themes, no 'World's Best Mom' type items) - textbook generic-catalog-under-a-holiday-label mislabeling, the exact anti-pattern flagged in this task's instructions. (4) /rooms/valentine-gifts.html, /father-s-day-gift-guide.html (4 items: glass mugs + passport cover), /christmas-gifts-for-women.html (4 items: keychains + mug), /christmas-gifts-under-999.html (4 items: lap trays), /secret-santa-gifting-ideas.html (4 items: iPad sleeves), /easy-holiday-makeover.html (3 items: cushion cover, tray, table runner) - all are small fixed curated grids of plainly generic, non-occasion-specific merchandise (no Santa/tree/ornament motifs, no heart/romance motifs, no fatherhood-specific items) - editorial gift-guide landing pages, excluded per the blog/lookbook/gift-guide boundary rule. No trace anywhere in the sitemap or nav of Holi, Eid, Thanksgiving, Halloween, Easter, New Year, or Hanukkah categories - confirmed absent (not just zero-search-result absent; the full 231-URL collections sitemap and page sitemap were enumerated and title-scanned for these terms, none found). /women-s-day.html and /housewarming-gifts.html exist but are out of this task's holiday scope (not seasonal per the defined list) and were left out accordingly.
